summary_paragraph: The patient with a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by hypoglycemia requiring 24-hour tube feeds and gastrostomy tube (recently reversed) presented with 4 days of burning epigastric pain similar to prior gastritis/ulcer symptoms and right upper extremity pain at the PICC insertion site used for IV pantoprazole. Evaluation for PICC complications included an upper extremity venous ultrasound negative for DVT and blood cultures that showed no growth. With symptom improvement in the hospital and ability to tolerate a bariatric stage III diet along with tube feeds, and given lack of expected benefit from IV PPI plus ongoing PICC site pain, the PICC was removed and she was transitioned back to oral pantoprazole twice daily with continuation of sucralfate and home medications. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable with return precautions and surgical follow-up arranged.
